finding.claim: Broken object-level authorization (IDOR): GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns any invoice by ID with no authentication or ownership check. The sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> enforces inv["customer"] == g.user["id"], so this route bypasses the intended control.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled URL path parameter inv_id, from any requester (no auth precondition visible).
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and other invoice data, for any customer.

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) looks up the record by the caller-supplied ID; only a 404 check follows.
The invoice is returned without comparing inv["customer"] to g.user. Compare line 16, where the check exists in the /my/ variant.

finding.guards_checked: No before_request or auth decorator in the file. g.user is never referenced on this route. No ownership or role check. The only other file-level control is the 404 on a missing ID. Only invoices.py exists in the directory, so I could not check for global middleware, and the app does not set g.user itself. If invoice IDs are sequential or guessable, enumeration is trivial.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a 404 on missing ID at invoices.py:9; no auth decorator, before_request, or ownership check; no other app code exists to supply global middleware)
verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 serves any invoice by caller-supplied ID with no auth or ownership check, while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 enforces inv["customer"] != g.user["id"], so any anonymous requester can read other customers' invoices.

verdict_facts.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no decorator and returns INVOICES.get(inv_id) via jsonify with only a 404 check, while the sibling at invoices.py:16 enforces inv["customer"] != g.user["id"]; the route is reachable by any HTTP client and the directory has no other controls.
